version.description:
Make a little progress, every day. Day in Ink gives your daily habits a simple place to live, with colorful cards, quick check-ins, and clear trends.

- Track numeric goals such as steps, minutes, or glasses of water.
- Add progress with a tap or enter an exact daily total.
- Track pass/fail habits with your choice of passed or failed as the daily default.
- Switch a habit between numeric progress and pass/fail while keeping recorded history.
- Review previous days and correct your history.
- Explore 7-, 30-, and 90-day trends, completion rates, and streaks.
- Archive habits while keeping their history.
- Export a backup and import it to restore habits and history.

Your habits stay in the app's storage on your iPhone. No account, ads, or analytics. App data may be included in your device backups. Exported backups are not encrypted by the app.

Support: https://apps.droessmj.com/day-in-ink/support.html
Privacy policy: https://apps.droessmj.com/day-in-ink/privacy.html

app_privacy.basis: The native app stores and processes habit data on-device, with no analytics SDK or developer-operated network service. User-selected exported files and Apple device backups are separately controlled. External website analytics is disclosed in the policy; the native app does not embed the support website. Confirm this remains true for the final uploaded build.

app_review.notes: No account or sign-in is required. A fresh installation starts with editable habits and no fabricated check-in history. Tap + on Walk twice, relaunch, and verify progress persists. Open a pass/fail habit and test Passed, Failed, and Clear this day. Edit a habit's Daily default; unrecorded days use that default, including past days, while explicit check-ins remain unchanged. Switching tracking type preserves recorded days' original type, goal, and unit; clearing a recorded day adopts current settings. In Habits > About > Export and import, export a backup, modify progress, import the backup, review it, and confirm replacement. Import replaces all current data; cancellation and rejected files leave existing data unchanged. Version 1 backups ask for their original calendar before conversion; new backups use stable Gregorian day keys. Help & Support and Privacy Policy are accessible in About and the recovery flow.

testflight.what_to_test: Daily numeric totals and small fractional values; pass/fail defaults and overrides; tracking-type changes with existing history; export/import, cancellation and restore; old-backup calendar migration; history after calendar preference changes and clock rollback; support/privacy links; VoiceOver and large text.

version.description:
Filter unwanted texts with keywords you choose. Blotter checks eligible messages from unknown senders on your iPhone and sends keyword matches to Junk.

- Add keywords or phrases to your own filtering rules.
- Choose case-sensitive, accent-sensitive, or whole-word matching.
- Process messages on your iPhone without sending message text to a developer-operated server.

Enable Blotter in iPhone Settings before using it. Filtering applies only to messages iOS provides to third-party text filters; iMessage and messages from Contacts are excluded. Matching is based on your chosen text rules, so broad keywords can also match legitimate messages.

Blotter does not keep a message or keyword-match history. No account, ads, or analytics SDK is required.

Support: https://apps.droessmj.com/blotter/support.html
Privacy policy: https://apps.droessmj.com/blotter/privacy.html

app_privacy.basis: The native app and embedded filter process message bodies and rules on-device without sending them off-device or recording match history. Cleanup only deletes legacy data. External website analytics is disclosed separately; the native app does not embed the support website. Confirm the final app and extension privacy reports and all SDKs.

app_review.notes: No account or sign-in is required. This app embeds the IdentityLookup message filter com.droessmj.blotter.filter; the extension does not have a separate store listing. In iPhone Settings > Apps > Messages, find text-message filtering and select Blotter. Return to Blotter and add pineapple with default whole-word matching. From an unknown sender not in Contacts, send an eligible SMS containing pineapple offer; it should be classified as Junk. A message containing hello there should receive no classification from Blotter. Do not use iMessage for this test. iOS controls message eligibility. No Activity tab or message/match history exists. Help & Support and Privacy Policy links are accessible during setup and on the Keywords screen. The new bundle ID is a separate installation from development builds using com.droessmj.sift; select the new Blotter filter explicitly. Shared preferences remain in the existing App Group, and the containing app retains only scoped deletion access to legacy Keychain data.

testflight.what_to_test: Filter setup and explicit selection of the new app; eligible unknown-sender SMS/MMS matches and nonmatches; case/accent/whole-word settings; rule edits reaching the extension; Contacts/iMessage exclusions; locked-device behavior after first unlock; legacy cleanup and preservation of shared rules; support/privacy links and large text.

capabilities.identity_note: New app identity, not an in-place update to com.droessmj.sift. Keep the same developer team and App Group to access shared rules. Private containers belonging to the old app/extension cannot be read or cleaned by the new identities; remove old installations separately after confirming rules and selecting the new filter.
